data.name: Ekaterina
data.gender_notes: Ekaterina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'Aikaterine', derived from 'Aikaterinos', meaning 'pure' or 'clear'. In Christianity, Saint Catherine of Alexandria is the patron saint of scholars and unmarried women. She is believed to have converted to Christianity through visions and was known for her wisdom and purity. The name Ekaterina carries the meaning “Pure, Clear, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ekaterina usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clear, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ekaterina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clear, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekaterina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: אקטרינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אקטרינה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'אקאטה', שפירושה טהורה וקדושה. הוא קשור למושגים של טהרה רוחנית ופיזית, ומהווה השראה לנוצרים לחיות חיים של קדושה וצדקה.

in_greek.name: Εκατερίνη
in_greek.meaning: Καθαρή και Άγια σε Πνεύμα και Σώμα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Εκατερίνη προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'ακάθιστος', που σημαίνει 'αμόλυντος' ή 'αγνός'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της πνευματικής και σωματικής καθαρότητας, και αποτελεί σύμβολο της αρετής και της αγιότητας.

in_latin.name: Ekaterina
in_latin.meaning: Pura et Sancta in Spiritu et Corpore
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ekaterina derivatur ex voce Graeca 'ακάθιστος', quae significat 'immundus' vel 'sanctus'. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc refertur ad conceptum puritatis spiritualis et corporalis, et est symbolum virtutis et sanctitatis.
